data.name: Web3 / Wallet / NFT Surface
data.description: Blockchain/web3 endpoints handling wallet addresses, NFT minting, and on-chain key material (ethers). Internet-facing crypto-asset surface with its own key-handling and ownership-verification trust boundary.

threats.title: [F-033] Hardcoded BIP39 wallet mnemonic (routes/checkKeys.ts:10)
threats.description:
A twelve-word BIP39 mnemonic is embedded as a source literal at routes/checkKeys.ts:10 and expanded into a full HD wallet at line 11, so anyone reading the repository derives the private key, public key, and address of that wallet without touching the running application and can sign transactions moving every asset the wallet holds.

Impact: The seed controls the entire derived key tree, so every asset held by that wallet is transferable by any reader of the source, and the compromise cannot be contained without abandoning the wallet.

Risk: High (likelihood High, impact High)
CWE: CWE-798
CVSS v4: 9.3 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N)
Evidence tier: confirmed-exploitable
Source: stride

Evidence:
routes/checkKeys.ts:10 assigns the complete mnemonic phrase as a plaintext string constant used by HDNodeWallet.fromPhrase on line 11.
- routes/checkKeys.ts:10

Full finding: threat-model.md#f-033 (F-033)
threats.mitigation:
M-033 — Move secrets to a managed secret store (priority P2, effort Medium)
1. Delete the literal at routes/checkKeys.ts:10, load the phrase from an environment-supplied secret at startup, and fail startup when it is absent so no fallback value ships.
2. Rotate to a freshly generated wallet, purge the exposed one, and add a repository secret-scanning check that fails CI on a BIP39 phrase in tracked source.
Verification: Start the application without the seed environment variable and confirm startup fails; grep the tracked tree for the old phrase and confirm zero hits.
Reference: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

threats.title: [F-044] Unverified wallet ownership claim (routes/nftMint.ts:41)
threats.description:
An attacker posts any wallet address to POST /rest/web3/walletNFTVerify; routes/nftMint.ts:41 reads req.body.walletAddress and line 42 treats mere membership in the addressesMinted set as proof that the caller controls that address. No signed message or nonce challenge binds the request to the private key, so an attacker who observes a minting address on the public Sepolia chain claims the mint result of a wallet they do not own, and the delete at line 43 also consumes that wallet's pending record.

Impact: On-chain identity is spoofable at the API boundary: mint attestations are credited to the wrong party and a legitimate wallet's pending verification record is destroyed by an unrelated caller.

Risk: Medium (likelihood High, impact Medium)
CWE: CWE-290
Evidence tier: confirmed-exploitable
Source: stride

Evidence:
routes/nftMint.ts:41 takes the wallet identity straight from the request body, with no signature verification anywhere in the handler.
- routes/nftMint.ts:41

Trust boundary crossings:
- tb-1 external → api-backend (internet-facing): The Internet-to-REST-API boundary assumes JWT authentication runs before the handler, but this wallet identity claim crosses it with no authenticated subject at all.

Full finding: threat-model.md#f-044 (F-044)
threats.mitigation:
M-044 — Require signed nonce proof of wallet control (priority P3, effort Medium)
1. Issue a server-generated nonce, require the client to return an EIP-191 signature over it, and in routes/nftMint.ts recover the signer with ethers verifyMessage before consulting addressesMinted.
2. Add a test that posts a valid minted address without a matching signature and asserts the response reports failure and leaves addressesMinted unchanged.
Verification: POST /rest/web3/walletNFTVerify with a known minted address and no signature field returns success:false and a follow-up request from the real owner still succeeds.
Reference: CWE-290: Authentication Bypass by Spoofing

threats.title: [F-045] Open redirect via substring allowlist (routes/redirect.ts:19)
threats.description:
An unauthenticated attacker requests GET /redirect?to=https://evil.example/?x=https://github.com/juice-shop/juice-shop. The gate at routes/redirect.ts:16 delegates to security.isRedirectAllowed, which accepts any URL that merely contains an allowlisted string anywhere (lib/insecurity.ts:136 uses url.includes), so res.redirect at routes/redirect.ts:19 sends the victim a 302 to the attacker host under the application's own origin and link reputation.

Impact: Phishing and token-exfiltration campaigns inherit the shop's domain reputation; any secret carried in the Referer of the redirected navigation reaches the attacker host.

Risk: Medium (likelihood High, impact Medium)
CWE: CWE-601
Evidence tier: confirmed-exploitable
Source: stride

Evidence:
routes/redirect.ts:19 performs res.redirect(toUrl) on a value only screened by a containment test, not an exact-match or origin comparison.
- routes/redirect.ts:19

Full finding: threat-model.md#f-045 (F-045)
threats.mitigation:
M-045 — Validate redirect targets against an allowlist (priority P3, effort Low)
1. Parse toUrl with the WHATWG URL parser in routes/redirect.ts and accept it only when the parsed origin plus pathname exactly equals an allowlist entry, rejecting every other value with 406.
2. Add a route test asserting that /redirect?to=https://evil.example/?x=<allowlisted-url> returns 406 and emits no Location header.
Verification: curl -sI 'http://localhost:3000/redirect?to=https://evil.example/?x=https://github.com/juice-shop/juice-shop' returns HTTP/1.1 406 and no Location header.
Reference: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

threats.title: [F-050] Trusted external event state change (routes/web3Wallet.ts:29)
threats.description:
An attacker posts an arbitrary address to POST /rest/web3/walletExploitAddress, which routes/web3Wallet.ts:16 inserts into the module-global walletsConnected set before any check. The provider event handler then flips server-side challenge state at routes/web3Wallet.ts:29 as soon as the public Sepolia contract emits ContractExploited naming that address, so a third party's on-chain transaction — or any address the attacker pre-registers — mutates the application's security-relevant state without the attacker ever proving key control.

Impact: Server-side completion state is written from an untrusted external event stream, letting an attacker attribute another party's on-chain action to themselves and corrupting the integrity of the progress record.

Risk: Medium (likelihood Medium, impact Medium)
CWE: CWE-306
Evidence tier: confirmed-exploitable
Source: stride

Evidence:
routes/web3Wallet.ts:29 calls challengeUtils.solveIf with an unconditional predicate, gated only on membership in a set that unauthenticated request bodies populate at line 16.
- routes/web3Wallet.ts:29

Full finding: threat-model.md#f-050 (F-050)
threats.mitigation:
M-050 — Require authentication on every exposed endpoint (priority P3, effort Medium)
1. Register an address in walletsConnected only after the caller proves key control with a signed nonce, and key the entry to the authenticated session so the event handler at routes/web3Wallet.ts:26 resolves a specific subject.
2. Add a test that registers address A from one session and asserts a ContractExploited event for address A does not change state for a different session.
Verification: Emit a simulated ContractExploited event for an address registered without signature proof and assert the challenge state remains unsolved.
Reference: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

threats.title: [F-065] Raw error message disclosure (routes/nftMint.ts:33)
threats.description:
An unauthenticated caller triggers a provider failure on GET /rest/web3/nftMintListen; the catch block at routes/nftMint.ts:33 returns utils.getErrorMessage(error), which is the raw error.message (lib/utils.ts:211), to the client. Errors raised while constructing the WebSocketProvider carry the endpoint URL built at line 18, which embeds ALCHEMY_API_KEY, so internal configuration and potentially the provider API key surface in the HTTP response.

Impact: Reconnaissance data about the blockchain provider integration, and possibly the API key contained in the provider URL, reach an unauthenticated caller.

Risk: Medium (likelihood Medium, impact Medium)
CWE: CWE-209
Evidence tier: insecure-practice
Source: stride

Evidence:
routes/nftMint.ts:33 serializes the unfiltered runtime error text into the 500 response body instead of a generic message.
- routes/nftMint.ts:33

Full finding: threat-model.md#f-065 (F-065)
threats.mitigation:
M-065 — Return generic error messages to clients (priority P3, effort Low)
1. Replace the getErrorMessage payload in routes/nftMint.ts:33, routes/web3Wallet.ts:36, and routes/checkKeys.ts:30 with a fixed message plus a correlation id, and send the detail to the server log only.
2. Add a test that forces provider construction to throw and asserts the response body contains neither the provider host nor the API key value.
Verification: Unset ALCHEMY_API_KEY, force a provider error, and confirm the 500 body contains no 'alchemy.com' substring while the log does.
Reference: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

threats.title: [F-069] Unbounded in-memory address set (routes/web3Wallet.ts:16)
threats.description:
An unauthenticated attacker loops POST /rest/web3/walletExploitAddress with a distinct walletAddress each time; routes/web3Wallet.ts:16 adds every value to the module-global walletsConnected set before any validation, and entries are removed only when a matching on-chain event arrives. Nothing caps the set size, expires entries, or rate-limits the route, so process memory grows with request volume until the Node process degrades or is killed.

Impact: Sustained request volume from a single unauthenticated client exhausts heap memory and takes down the shared Express process serving the whole application.

Risk: Medium (likelihood Medium, impact Medium)
CWE: CWE-400
CVSS v4: 6.9 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N)
Evidence tier: confirmed-exploitable
Source: stride

Evidence:
routes/web3Wallet.ts:16 performs an unconditional Set.add of request-controlled data; a zero-hit search for rateLimit in the component files confirms no request-rate bound protects it.
- routes/web3Wallet.ts:16

Full finding: threat-model.md#f-069 (F-069)
threats.mitigation:
M-069 — Rate-limit expensive requests and bound input size (priority P3, effort Low)
1. Validate walletAddress against the 0x-prefixed 40-hex-character format, store entries in a bounded LRU or TTL map instead of an unbounded Set in routes/web3Wallet.ts, and apply express-rate-limit to the route registration.
2. Add a test that sends more distinct addresses than the configured cap and asserts the retained entry count stays at the cap.
Verification: Send 10000 distinct addresses and assert the tracked entry count equals the configured maximum and heap usage stays flat.
Reference: CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
